cursor.note: THE SEAL VOCABULARY'S AXIS IS WHETHER THE SEAL WAS ASKED FOR, which is why three of its four words are measurements and only `open` is the absence of one — and why `sealed -> open` is the single transition that retires a measurement rather than recording a newer one. On 2026-09-08 a blanket re-seal made that transition 44 times and nothing refused it; it was caught by diffing one file by hand. Two acts close it, because a guard alone would have punished a caller who meant the right thing: persist_validation now refuses sealed|indeterminate|breached -> open unless the caller states `unsealing_because`, which then rides permanently inside the record's evidence (the escape is on the record, never ambient) and fires BEFORE the announce and the write, so a refused write leaves the standing record untouched; and `cairn test --seal` asks each proof what isolation its standing seal was taken at and reproduces THAT, so the ordinary re-seal never meets the guard at all. sealed->breached, sealed->indeterminate and open->sealed all pass unrefused: a guard blocking a newer RED would be Law 7 inverted at the door Law 7 exists for. THE PER-PROOF READ IS VISIBLE AS A DISTRIBUTION rather than a word: the tester's own eight re-sealed at netns=4 none=4, the twelve out-of-component proofs fingerprinting a file this voyage changed at netns=11 none=1, and every one of the nineteen carrying a seal at HEAD reproduced it with zero guard refusals — including the three the blanket sweep had reddened and build_inspector's test_inspector, which carries seal:open because it times out at 120s inside a netns. One typed flag would have had to be wrong for one of those groups. A SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME FUNCTION was fixed here under ruling 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage: the --seal summary printed `total - n_red` persisted while its own next clause said 'a red seals its red' (49 proofs, 6 red, printed 43, 49 on disk) — a Law 7 lie misreporting the very count this ticket is about. Five teeth, green twice, both mutations bite. And two deviations from the chart are in the verdict rather than smoothed over: hypothesis 1's falsifier fixed a corpus SNAPSHOT where it meant an invariant, and the probe's `enough` holds a floor on the sealed COUNT where the spec named a RATIO — a ratio falls when someone honestly adds an unsealed proof, so it would poke the owner about the system working.

window.note: a seal snapshots the instance root ONCE per batch and leaves the trail tree empty — and the hollow green that fell out of it is fixed here too, by ruling. MEASURED BEFORE, by running HEAD's own snapshot code rather than remembering it: two full copies per sealed proof, 888.7MB / 9.28s / 163,352 entries before a single tooth ran. AFTER, same box same minute: 118.0MB / 0.34s / 3,620 entries for a batch's first proof and 0.09s for every proof after it. Three changes, each with its own tooth: the trail tree arrives EMPTY BUT PRESENT (73% of the bytes, and the DIRECTORY must survive or check_instance_seal reads every later seal INDETERMINATE); the live root is read once per PROCESS, the pristine invalidated on its TOP-LEVEL NAME SET because that is the one movement a stale pristine cannot survive; and ONE copy per proof rather than two, the seal's probe now clearing its own marker. The cost is on the record at every seal — evidence.instance_seal.scratch carries apparent bytes AND disk bytes AND entry count, because the old snapshot was 136MB of content sitting in 424MB of 4KB blocks: apparent alone understates 3x, disk alone hides that the cost is entry COUNT. That IS this ticket's watch, and it now fires on every seal. THE RE-SEAL SWEEP READ 200 PROOFS, 192 GREEN, 8 RED, and attribution was measured rather than argued: the tree was stashed, HEAD confirmed to carry the old two-copy isolation.py, and all 8 re-run there — 7 are red at HEAD too and belong to other tickets. THE EIGHTH WAS A HOLLOW GREEN THE EMPTIER SANDBOX EXPOSED. inference_domain's probe resolved its trail through TWO doors and only the first followed the device: diagnostic_trail() honoured the device's roots and set trail_exists, while a hand-built BreadcrumbLog with no roots supplied the records from the LIVE berth. Its tooth wrote one line into an isolated trail and asserted trail_misses >= 1 — a bound BOTH trails meet — so for two months it passed on the live trail's borrowed lines and never on the line it wrote. The seal did not break that proof; it removed the accident the proof was passing on. FIXED IN THIS VOYAGE BY RULING 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage (Akien: 'we are just going to attach that to the same ticket as a bug we fix with it'; confirmed 'agreed on all counts. ruled approved and boogied'). The fix is at the BASE CLASS, where the shape cannot come back: DiagnosticBase answered WHERE a device's records are and nothing answered WHAT they are, so the one caller that wanted the lines built its own address and half-followed the device. diagnostic_records() now sits beside diagnostic_trail(), both carrying roots=getattr(self,'_diagnostic_roots',None); inference_domain passes it through; the probe builds no address of its own; the tooth's bound is == 1. Measured both ways: fixed reads trail_misses=1, reverted reads 3312. Four new teeth in test_device_logs_unwired.py hold it and all bite under mutation. Trouble an-inference-call-probe-reads-two-different-trails cleared through its door. THE BOUNDS MOVED BY RULING AND THE BERTHED CHART PACKETS DID NOT — rewriting constrain's bounds.in afterward would make the record lie about what the chart knew when it was charted; the widening is recorded forward, in the ruling and in the verdict's findings.

window.note: The watch is armed at cairn/devices/tester/probes/seal_measurements_are_not_dropped.py, and its `enough` is written against a named precedent rather than a habit: a_pickup_is_witnessed.py clears on `pickups >= 1`, took its 1 pickup in August 2026, and has read green off a historical fact ever since. This one requires 30 elapsed days AND the sealed count at or above its arming baseline of 122 AND zero records carrying an `unsealing_because` — so at arming it reads enough=False, and a watch that can clear before it can fire is not a watch. It watches the two ways the fix can be lost: the escape becoming the route (escapes > 0), and measurements disappearing some other way (the sealed count falling below baseline). THE SHAPE DEVIATES FROM THE TICKET'S SPEC AND THE DEVIATION IS DELIBERATE: the spec named a sealed:open RATIO, and a ratio falls whenever someone honestly adds an unsealed proof — which this very voyage did — so a ratio watch would poke the owner about the system working correctly. The floor on the absolute sealed count only falls when a measurement went away.
